title: Classical coherence matrices and measurement scope

items.title: Classical two-component coherency matrix
items.physical_scope: An ideal classical ensemble of two complex transverse electric-field components at a specified plane in a fixed positively oriented SI laboratory chart, using the exp(-i omega t) convention and the cone specified in the Definition. Gamma is an uncentered second-moment matrix of the two-component projection; it is not a quantum density operator or a full three-dimensional coherence matrix. The paraxial suppliers bound longitudinal amplitude for individual exact plane modes but do not supply an aggregate ensemble or detector-error bound. No measurement, absolute radiometric calibration, sampling law, or empirical claim is made. A time average is not identified with the ensemble expectation without separately stated stationarity and ergodicity assumptions.
items.statement:
Fix a named, positively oriented SI laboratory chart with coordinates
$(x,y,z,t)$ and angular frequency $\omega>0$. Adopt the SI constants and
coordinate units of the laboratory convention: $c>0$ is in m s$^{-1}$,
$k_0:=\omega/c$ is in m$^{-1}$, and electric-field components are in V
m$^{-1}$. Let
$\Pi=\{(x,y,z_0):(x,y)\in D\}$ be a specified reference plane, where
$z_0\in\mathbb R$ and $D\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ is a specified nonempty region.
Its oriented orthonormal transverse basis is $(e_x,e_y)$ and its normal is
$e_z$.

For the paraxial context, adopt $c>0$, $k_0=\omega/c$, and
$0<\delta<1$. The angular-spectrum variable $\xi\in\mathbb R^2$ is measured
in cycles per metre, $q=2\pi\xi$ is in m$^{-1}$, and the forward propagating
cone is $D_\delta=\{\xi:|q|\le\delta k_0\}$ with
$k_z(\xi)=\sqrt{k_0^2-|q|^2}>0$. The matrix below is defined pointwise for the
two-component projection; it does not assert that an arbitrary random
superposition is an exact Maxwell field or that the individual-mode
longitudinal bound extends to an ensemble without additional hypotheses.

Let $(\Xi,\mathcal A,\mathbb P)$ be a specified probability space. At each
fixed $\rho\in D$, let $Z_\rho:\Xi\to\mathbb C^2$ be measurable, with four real
coordinates
$X_\rho=(\operatorname{Re}Z_x,\operatorname{Im}Z_x,
\operatorname{Re}Z_y,\operatorname{Im}Z_y)$ forming a square-integrable
$\mathbb R^4$ random vector and
$\mathbb E[|Z_x(\rho)|^2+|Z_y(\rho)|^2]<\infty$. For $\sigma\in\Xi$, the
associated transverse real-field model is
$E_\perp(\rho,\sigma,t)=\operatorname{Re}(Z_\rho(\sigma)e^{-i\omega t})$.
Expectation is taken over this declared classical ensemble and is applied
componentwise to complex integrable variables. Define
$$\Gamma(\rho):=\mathbb E[Z_\rho Z_\rho^\dagger],\qquad \Gamma_{ij}(\rho):=\mathbb E[Z_i(\rho)\overline{Z_j(\rho)}]\quad(i,j\in\{1,2\}).$$
Thus $\Gamma$ is the uncentered second-moment matrix of the two selected
components; no zero-mean assumption is made. The degree of polarization is
defined only when $S_0>0$ by
$$S_0:=\Gamma_{11}+\Gamma_{22},\quad S_1:=\Gamma_{11}-\Gamma_{22},\quad S_2:=2\operatorname{Re}\Gamma_{12},\quad S_3:=-2\operatorname{Im}\Gamma_{12},\qquad \mathcal P:=\frac{\sqrt{S_1^2+S_2^2+S_3^2}}{S_0}.$$
The minus sign in $S_3$ is fixed by the stated phasor convention and the
ordered basis $(e_x,e_y)$. In this two-component model, a positive-intensity
state is called unpolarized when $\Gamma=(S_0/2)I_2$; this label concerns
second moments and does not say that any realization is a quantum state.
The $S_j$ have units (V m$^{-1}$)$^2$; $S_0$ is a mean-square field coordinate,
not an absolutely calibrated irradiance.

The construction applies to any ordered pair of square-integrable classical
complex amplitudes. When the pair labels transverse electric components,
$S_j$ have the polarization interpretation just defined. When it labels two
beam channels, the same matrix entries are channel correlations; they are not
polarization components.

references.title: José J. Gil, Polarimetric Characterization of Light and Media, §2.1–2.6, author-revised 2020 version of Eur. Phys. J. Appl. Phys. 40 (2007)
references.locator: §2.1, PDF pp. 6–7: 2×2 coherency matrix from two complex field components and time versus ensemble averaging; §2.2–2.6, PDF pp. 7–11: Stokes coordinates, the positive-semidefinite cone and rank/purity. The local definition uses an ensemble expectation directly and does not import the source's zero-mean analytic-signal or stationary-ergodic interpretation as an extra assumption.

items.title: Stokes cone and deterministic Jones transformations
items.physical_scope: Conditional algebra for the classical two-component coherency matrix defined in this library. For transverse electric components its four real coordinates are the stated Stokes parameters; for other classical two-channel amplitudes the same cone is an algebraic second-moment constraint, not a polarization interpretation. No quantum-state identification, apparatus model, empirical observation, or finite-sample claim is made.
items.statement:
Let $Z=(Z_1,Z_2)^{\mathsf T}$ be a measurable square-integrable complex
two-component vector on a probability space and define
$\Gamma:=\mathbb E[ZZ^\dagger]$, with
$\Gamma_{ij}:=\mathbb E[Z_i\overline{Z_j}]$. Put
$S_0:=\Gamma_{11}+\Gamma_{22}$,
$S_1:=\Gamma_{11}-\Gamma_{22}$,
$S_2:=2\operatorname{Re}\Gamma_{12}$, and
$S_3:=-2\operatorname{Im}\Gamma_{12}$; when $S_0>0$, put
$\mathcal P:=\sqrt{S_1^2+S_2^2+S_3^2}/S_0$. Then $\Gamma$ is positive
semidefinite, meaning
$v^\dagger\Gamma v\ge0$ for every $v\in\mathbb C^2$; its rank is the complex
dimension of its image. The Stokes coordinates satisfy
$$S_0\ge0,\qquad S_0^2\ge S_1^2+S_2^2+S_3^2.$$
Equality in the second relation holds exactly when $\Gamma=0$ or $\Gamma$ has
rank one. Consequently $\mathcal P\in[0,1]$ when $S_0>0$, and it is undefined
when $S_0=0$. If a fixed deterministic dimensionless complex-linear map
$M:\mathbb C^2\to\mathbb C^2$ (a Jones matrix in this model) sends each
realization $Z$ to $MZ$, then
$\Gamma$ transforms to $M\Gamma M^\dagger$.

references.title: José J. Gil, Polarimetric Characterization of Light and Media, §2.1–2.6, author-revised 2020 version of Eur. Phys. J. Appl. Phys. 40 (2007)
references.locator: §2.1–2.3, PDF pp. 6–10: Hermitian 2×2 coherency matrices, Pauli/Stokes coordinates, positivity cone and rank-one purity. The local proof derives each inequality directly and fixes its $S_3$ sign from the repository phasor convention.

items.title: Visibility bound in a specified two-beam model
items.physical_scope: Conditional result for an ideal scalar two-beam classical phasor model with a common ensemble, finite second moments, a controllable full relative-phase sweep, and mean-square amplitude as the detector-response model. The $\Gamma_{12}$ here is the cross-moment between two beam channels; it is not the transverse-polarization cross-component of one beam. The visibility is the model contrast, not a finite-sample estimate. No detector calibration, noise model, empirical observation, or unconditional claim about measured fringe visibility is made.
items.statement:
Let $A_1,A_2:\Xi\to\mathbb C$ be jointly measurable classical phasor amplitudes
at one fixed observation point for a single selected scalar field component,
on one probability space, each in V m$^{-1}$, with
$\mathbb E(|A_1|^2+|A_2|^2)<\infty$. Define
$I_j:=\mathbb E[|A_j|^2]$ and
$\Gamma_{12}:=\mathbb E[A_1\overline{A_2}]$. Adopt the ideal scalar
two-beam model with a phase multiplier ranging over the full unit circle
$\mathbb T:=\{\zeta\in\mathbb C:|\zeta|=1\}$. For each $\zeta\in\mathbb T$,
set $A_\zeta:=A_2+\zeta A_1$ and $I(\zeta):=\mathbb E[|A_\zeta|^2]$.
The quantities $I_j$ and $I(\zeta)$
are mean-square field coordinates in (V m$^{-1}$)$^2$, not calibrated
irradiances. Set
$I_{\max}:=\max_{\zeta\in\mathbb T}I(\zeta)$ and
$I_{\min}:=\min_{\zeta\in\mathbb T}I(\zeta)$. When $I_1+I_2>0$, define the
model visibility by
$$V:=\frac{I_{\max}-I_{\min}}{I_{\max}+I_{\min}}.$$
Then
$$I(\zeta)=I_1+I_2+2\operatorname{Re}(\zeta\Gamma_{12}),\qquad V=\frac{2|\Gamma_{12}|}{I_1+I_2}\le1.$$

references.title: José J. Gil, Polarimetric Characterization of Light and Media, §2.1–2.3, author-revised 2020 version of Eur. Phys. J. Appl. Phys. 40 (2007)
references.locator: §2.1–2.3, PDF pp. 6–10: second-moment coherency matrices and their positive-semidefinite/Stokes constraints; the local item applies this matrix construction to two beam channels without identifying them with polarization axes.

references.title: Optics Lectures, University of Oxford, 2012, sections on coherence and interferometers
references.locator: PDF pp. 9–10, 'Coherence' and 'Interferometers': slow-detector mean intensity, cross-correlation term, phase extrema, and fringe-visibility formula.

references.title: A. Hemmerich, Lectures on Classical Optics, Part III (2023)
references.locator: PDF pp. 2–4, 'The concept of coherence' and 'Interference visibility': normalized pair correlation, mean intensity, visibility, and the equal-intensity special case.

title: Classical coherence matrices and measurement scope — Examples

items.title: Mixed classical polarization ensembles
items.physical_scope: A finite, ideal classical ensemble of two transverse electric phasors at a fixed paraxial detector point. The example distinguishes a vanishing ensemble polarization vector from nonzero field amplitude in every realization. It is a constructed model example, not a reported preparation, measurement, or observation and not a quantum density-operator interpretation.
items.statement:
At one fixed detector point, let a nonzero complex electric amplitude $a$,
with units V m$^{-1}$, occur with equal probability in the two realizations
$Z=(a,0)^{\mathsf T}$ and $Z=(0,a)^{\mathsf T}$. Then
$\Gamma=(|a|^2/2)I_2$, $S_0=|a|^2>0$, and $S_1=S_2=S_3=0$, so the ensemble is
unpolarized by the two-component definition even though each realization is
a definite nonzero classical field amplitude.

references.title: José J. Gil, Polarimetric Characterization of Light and Media, §2.1–2.6, author-revised 2020 version of Eur. Phys. J. Appl. Phys. 40 (2007)
references.locator: §2.1–2.6, PDF pp. 6–11: classical second-moment coherency matrices, unpolarized states, and Stokes coordinates. The finite ensemble and its amplitudes are constructed and computed locally.

items.title: Normalized polarization is undefined at darkness
items.physical_scope: A zero-amplitude classical ensemble in the two-component coherency-matrix model. It demonstrates a boundary of a normalization definition; it is not a reported dark-detector observation, a noise model, or an empirical claim.
items.statement:
For every square-integrable two-component classical ensemble, the quotient
$\mathcal P=\sqrt{S_1^2+S_2^2+S_3^2}/S_0$ defines a real degree of
polarization.

references.title: José J. Gil, Polarimetric Characterization of Light and Media, §2.1–2.6, author-revised 2020 version of Eur. Phys. J. Appl. Phys. 40 (2007)
references.locator: §2.1–2.6, PDF pp. 6–11: coherency matrices, Stokes coordinates and intensity/purity normalization. The zero-field boundary case is computed locally.
